transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-15 14:00 PDT | Duration: ~47m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Sam (Redwood CSM), Nina (Catalyst Head of ML), Evan (SRE), Priya (Product), Tom (Finance)

Summary: Quick QBR focused on usage trends (up 28% month-over-month), cost spikes in June during a marketing campaign, recent 2 short reliability blips (5-7 min) attributed to autoscaling config, and roadmap items that affect Catalyst (KV cache improvements, batching heuristics, Dedicated sizing). Action items and follow-ups agreed.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off, is that right, uh, everyone here?
[00:10] Nina: yep hi Maya, thanks, excited to see the numbers.
[00:15] Sam: quick note, agenda is usage/costs, reliability incidents, roadmap, then next steps.
[00:22] Priya: sounds good.
[00:30] Maya: cool, first up usage, we saw a steady growth you mentioned you launched the summer promo, that's reflected in tokens and requests, Jordan do you want to share the perf view?
[00:40] Jordan: yeah uh so we pulled the dashboards, overall qps up 32% week over week during the promo window, average seq length inching to 620 tokens, so that changes batch behavior and cost, we also noticed a small tail of long-running requests causing some worker saturation.
[01:05] Evan: right we saw a few spikes, our infra metrics show 3 times where latency climbed above 800ms, two of those were during autoscale cooldowns.
[01:18] Jordan: exactly, the cooldown and the warmup for Dedicated nodes -- well for hosted routing we fell back to additional cold instances which added latency. Not a model issue, more infra config.
[01:30] Tom: from finance side, June bill was 42% higher than forecast, the promo doubled inference volume, we thought caching would mitigate but maybe not enough.
[01:44] Maya: yeah this is where Redwood Optimize recommendations help, we have some tuning steps to reduce per-token bill. Sam, can you cover the ops recommendations?
[01:52] Sam: sure, main things are: enable prefix KV caching for high-frequency prompts, set smart batching window to 40ms for your seq distribution, and consider a cross-route cache for repeated system prompts. Also, we can run an A/B with quantized variant for lower-criticality routes.
[02:15] Priya: the quantized variant, does that change quality much for customer-facing flows? we've got some UX constraints.
[02:23] Jordan: typically the 4-bit quantized run shows small regressions on certain tokens but for short assistant responses it's within tolerance; we'd suggest a canary on non-critical routes first.
[02:33] Nina: ok, but we need to keep latency under 300ms p95 for checkout flows.
[02:40] Jordan: yes, for those critical routes we'd recommend pinning to the hosted low-latency pool or Dedicated. There's tradeoff cost vs latency.
[02:50] Evan: question, Dedicated sizing - if we move some routes to Dedicated, do we still get autoscaling benefits?
[02:57] Maya: Dedicated has reserved capacity with configurable autoscale and burst policies; Jordan can lay out throughput per instance and recommended commit levels.
[03:06] Jordan: for your peak observed load (~460 qps at 620 tokens avg) we'd estimate needing X G4dn-equivalent slots or equivalent A100 mounts, but we'll run a formal worksheet.
[03:24] Tom: okay the finance ask is: give us a commit vs on-demand comparison for next quarter, include projected savings.
[03:33] Maya: yes we'll send that.
[03:36] [03:36] Sam: quick note on reliability - you had two short blips in June, Jordan can walk through logs, but root cause was autoscale cooldown and an unusual cache eviction pattern.
[03:48] Jordan: the trace shows KV cache entry churn when request patterns changed during the promo; some large prefixes evicted smaller hot entries triggering extra compute. We're releasing a KV cache policy tweak in the next release to reduce that.
[04:05] Nina: that's good to hear, how soon?
[04:09] Sam: slated for late July rollout in the managed hosted environment; we'll prioritize your account earlier in the rollout schedule.
[04:17] [04:17] Priya: roadmap -- anything coming that materially changes cost or perf in Q3?
[04:22] Maya: yes, two big items: 1) improved batching heuristics that reduce wasted tokens for mid-length sequences, 2) quantization profile tooling so you can evaluate lower-cost models easily. Both targeted in Q3.
[04:37] Jordan: also KV cache improvements I mentioned and a new per-route cache TTL override for enterprises.
[04:45] Priya: per-route TTL override, that will help checkout route.
[04:49] Tom: any compliance or security items new? we need the KMS integration docs for procurement.
[04:55] Sam: we'll send the KMS integration guide and SOC2 whitepaper, also a snippet on SSO/SAML config for audit.
[05:04] Tom: great.
[05:06] [05:06] Maya: let's go deep on the billing breakdown -- Jordan do you have the per-route token counts?
[05:12] Jordan: yes, top three routes account for 76% of tokens: cart-summary, product-reco, checkout-helper; cart-summary alone jumped 3x during promo. We've got a suggested cache-on-read for cart-summary to cut tokens.
[05:28] Nina: cart-summary is candidates heavy, we do multi-pass ranking, can caching be done pre-rerank?
[05:34] Jordan: potentially, caching prefix outputs from the first-pass can avoid full model runs on repeat views. We'll prototype.
[05:42] Priya: any risk to freshness? we need user-specific content.
[05:46] Jordan: we'd recommend hybrid caching: user-scoped TTL of 2 minutes plus invalidation on cart change.
[05:52] [05:52] Evan: performance question: what's the expected p95 after applying 40ms batching and cache?
[05:57] Jordan: conservative estimate is 20-30% latency reduction p95 and 35% token reduction on high-hit routes.
[06:06] Tom: that helps. finance wants the numbers in a spreadsheet.
[06:10] Maya: we'll attach a worksheet with projected costs.
[06:13] [06:13] Sam: also want to flag upcoming infra maintenance window in Aug that could affect hosted routing; we'll schedule avoid windows with your peak.
[06:22] Nina: please do.
[06:25] [06:25] Maya: switching to Dedicated discussion quickly, Jordan?
[06:29] Jordan: Dedicated gives you predictable unit economics, you can pin models, and enforce private networking. For your SLA needs on checkout we can put checkout-helper on Dedicated and keep other routes hosted. We recommend a mix.
[06:44] Priya: what's the onboarding timeline for Dedicated?
[06:47] Jordan: typical timeline is 4-6 weeks from commit: sizing, security review, provisioning, and pilot. If you need faster we can do a hybrid pilot on reserved hosted nodes.
[06:57] Tom: procurement will need contract and pricing by July 22.
[07:02] Maya: we'll aim for that.
[07:05] [07:05] Sam: security checklist items: SOC2, SSO, KMS, VPC peering for Dedicated; we have templates.
[07:13] Tom: good.
[07:15] [07:15] Nina: any known upcoming breaking changes or model deprecations?
[07:19] Jordan: nothing major in Q3; we will announce deprecations at least 90 days ahead. We'll share a model catalog snapshot.
[07:28] [07:28] Maya: quick live Q&A from Evan on autoscale configs?
[07:32] Evan: yeah, what's the recommended cooldown for your autoscaler? we had issues with 60s cooldown.
[07:37] Jordan: recommend 300s cooldown for scale-down in high-variance workloads, and aggressive warmups on scale-up; also enable burst capacity of 15% for sudden promos.
[07:49] Evan: okay.
[07:51] [07:51] Priya: folks, just to be clear, who's owning the Dedicated sizing doc?
[07:56] Maya: Jordan will own it, Maya will coordinate with finance.
[08:01] [08:01] Tom: and billing breakdown? Maya.
[08:04] Maya: yes.
[08:06] [08:06] Sam: any blockers from Catalyst side?
[08:09] Nina: just finalizing peak qps numbers and sequence distributions, Evan will send.
[08:14] Evan: yep will do.
[08:16] [08:16] Maya: ok quick recap of action items: we'll send billing CSV, Dedicated sizing worksheet, SOC2 + KMS docs, and prototype caching suggestions. Any final Qs?
[08:29] Priya: timeline is tight but doable.
[08:33] Tom: fine.
[08:35] [08:35] Maya: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and the next meeting invite for the sizing workshop.
[08:42] Nina: thanks.
[08:45] [47:00] call ended

Notes: Transcript contains occasional transcription artifacts; proper nouns and acronyms may be slightly off. Shared artifacts referenced: billing CSV (link to be sent), Dedicated sizing worksheet (link to be created), SOC2 whitepaper (attachment), KMS integration guide (attachment).
